# CyclicPermutations

*The permutations of $[n]$ that are a single $n$-cycle, in one-line notation.*

## Usage

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\operatorname{CyclicPermutations}(n)$ | all $(n-1)!$ full $n$-cycles on $[n]$ |
| $\operatorname{At}(\operatorname{CyclicPermutations}(n),\ i)$ | the $n$-cycle at 1-based position $i$ |

## Details

- **Arity:** 1 — the ground size $n$.
- **Element:** a permutation (one-line) whose cycle structure is one cycle of length $n$. `[2, 3, 4, 1]` is the cycle $(1\,2\,3\,4)$.
- **Result type:** `collection` of `list<integer>`, each of length $n$.
- **Count:** $(n-1)!$ — fixing $1$ as the cycle's start and arranging the other $n-1$ (`CyclicPermutationCount`).
- **Order:** the cycle is written $(1,\,p)$ where $p = \operatorname{PermutationUnrank}(n-1, r)$ arranges $\{2, \dots, n\}$; the one-line image is read off that cycle (`CyclicPermutationUnrank`/`Rank`).
- **Random access:** $O(n)$ — one Lehmer decode plus a cycle-to-image pass.

## Examples

$\operatorname{Count}(\operatorname{CyclicPermutations}(4)) = 6$

The 6 four-cycles in rank order (one-line) are $[2, 3, 4, 1], [2, 4, 1, 3], [3, 4, 2, 1], [3, 1, 4, 2], [4, 3, 1, 2], [4, 1, 2, 3]$ — the first, $[2, 3, 4, 1]$, is the cycle $(1\,2\,3\,4)$.
